findings.code_evidence: return { id: p.id, name: p.name, sector: p.sector, country: p.country, stage: p.stage };
findings.reason: Project list responses use toSummary, which omits linked_companies and other upstream-only fields. The detail response also uses toDetail, which omits linked_companies.
On detected conflicts, the handler returns 409 with edit_conflict, current, and conflicting_fields, and does not call putProject before that branch.
The merge logic compares key_dates as one whole value, so the entire array is treated as a single merge/conflict field.

findings.code_evidence: const saved = await putProject(id, result.merged, current.linked_companies);
findings.reason: The full upstream PUT body includes linked_companies taken from the latest read current.linked_companies.
Missing projects are translated to HTTP 404 with project_not_found for both GET and PUT paths.
The PUT body must contain exactly base and proposed, each validated as EditableFields; extras are rejected by the exact key-count checks and invalid values fail validation.
The server exposes GET /api/projects, GET /api/projects/{id}, and PUT /api/projects/{id}.
The upstream API key is read from server environment and only used in upstreamFetch headers; it is never included in browser API responses.
Unavailable upstream reads are mapped to HTTP 502 with upstream_unavailable.
After a failed PUT, the handler performs at most one diagnostic getProject read and then returns 504 write_uncertain without retrying the write.
When the merged editable fields equal current, changed is false and the code returns 200 without calling putProject.
Invalid JSON or invalid request bodies are rejected with HTTP 422.
